**Conversation Overview**

This conversation represents Chat 24 of an ongoing long-form book production project called "The Method 1.6," a multi-volume technical work with a tightly controlled editorial and build system. The person is the author/project lead overseeing the production of six volumes: a main volume, a Register, a Mathematical Compendium, a Physics Compendium, an Index of Indices (IoI), and a Spectra Compendium. The project uses a structured handoff system between chat sessions, with a reading gate (§0) that must be executed before any other work, a working register (WORKING-REGISTER.md) tracking editorial decisions, and a formal ruling system (Rulings 1–42 plus an R27 Amendment) governing all changes. The Register contains 1,449 entry headings, 1,474 distinct numbers ranging 165–1770, and 24 Python instruments control the build pipeline.

The primary accomplishment of Chat 24 was completing the press across all six volumes after five sessions of deferred debt, with the figures archive finally fetched from Google Drive (file ID `1q7pvnxMPILD9AVoH6XjymZHXX79YzITd`, 6,299,293 bytes). All six volumes pressed successfully: main 281 pages, Register 388 pages, Mathematical Compendium 101 pages, Physics Compendium 26 pages, Index of Indices 42 pages, and Spectra Compendium 23 pages. Two defects in Appendix G were found and repaired — both invisible to structural checks and only detectable by reading the pressed PDF. First, `index_pages.py` hardcoded appendix letters as `[A-F]`, causing Appendix G to be silently dropped from the Contents while the press reported all headings mapped correctly. Second, a bare `|X|` in table row 1.7 was parsed as cell delimiters by pandoc, truncating the row and dropping the object `A.derived` from the printed table entirely. Both were repaired (generalizing to `[A-Z]`, escaping to `\|X\|`), and all 30 table locators were verified on the page. BUILD-25 was packed at 2 + 85 = 87 members, with `*.pages.md` derived press files newly excluded by suffix from bundling. Four gate errors were found inside HANDOFF-25 itself, and several probe faults occurred during Claude's own execution, all caught before reporting.

The person posed a standing question about whether the 47 uncited sections of a document called Transitions should ever enter the work whole, and if so, whether they belong in the Index of Indices rather than as a main-volume appendix. Claude agreed the IoI is the taxonomically correct location, while noting that this would constitute those sections entering the work — superseding part of Register entry 1770 — requiring a new Register entry rather than any edit to 1770. Two rulings remain open for the author: whether an editorial volume change (the pipe escape) requires a Register entry, and where the complete transition table should go. Three of four planned work items went unstarted for the fourth consecutive session — the twelve standing questions, Ruling 42's 29-line site list, and reader reads A4/A5/A6.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive large-file downloads for files over approximately 1 MB do not arrive inline; the result is written to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<tool_call_id>.json`. The correct decode sequence is: `d=json.load(open(p)); inner=json.loads(d[0]['text']); blob=base64.b64decode(inner['content'])`, followed by verification against the Drive `fileSize` field. The figures archive at file ID `1q7pvnxMPILD9AVoH6XjymZHXX79YzITd` is 6,299,293 bytes and sha256 prefix `ee423b9ca550a94e7fe0baa41f6ef032`; it unpacks to `figures/` (49 files) and `figures-compendia/` (12 files) and must be refetched each session as it is not a bundle member. `xxd` is not installed in this environment; terminal newline testing must use `od -An -tx1` instead, as a missing tool fails silently and returns output shaped like a valid answer. `

content.text:
## THE READING GATE — CERTIFICATE

```
CERT: chats read = 23/23 · bundle members = 2 + 84 = 86
      · rulings = 1–42 + amendment
      · Register entry headings = 1,449 · Register numbers = 1,474 (all distinct)
      · instruments = 24
G5:   grep -c 'App. G' <Math> = 32          [expected 32]  PASS
      grep -c 'W-019' WORKING-REGISTER.md = 1 [expected >=1] PASS
      BUILD IDENTITY CONFIRMED — this is BUILD-24.
```

**Gate errors found — four, three in the gate and one mine.**

1. G1 says 21 chats; its own list totals 22; the tool returns 23.
2. §0 records BUILD-24 bundle 2 at 83; it measures **84**. The extra is `HANDOFF-25.md` — the handoff packed into the build it describes, uncounted by the pack that wrote it.
3. §0 records the Register at 5,895 lines. It is **5,869** (`wc -l` 5868). The structure is untouched — 1,449 / 1,474 / 7 grouped / 4 subheads / 165–1770, with 1769 and 1770 present — so this is a wrong figure in the handoff, not a damaged volume.
4. §0 says WORKING-REGISTER.md does *not* carry Rulings 29 and 30. It **does** — verbatim, bold inline at lines 736 and 785. My first probe missed them because I grepped `Ruling 34` against a file that writes `RULING 34`. Case-sensitive probe, my fault, caught before I reported it.

`xxd` is not installed; my first newline test failed silently and reported every file identically. Redone with `od`: `Transitions.md` alone ends `0a`. §0 is right on that point.

W-015 does have no `###` heading — my probe found one only because `W-015a` at line 1721 contains the substring. That is the same substring fault as `T\s§` matching "AT" — **fourth consecutive session** an unguarded match nearly produced a false finding. Recording it now rather than at the close.

Gate passed. Opening the press.

### W-013 — coords.py HOOKED INTO build.py; ref.docx REBUILT AND ITS RECIPE CORRECTED (chat 19, BUILD-20)
**THE GATE IS HOOKED.** `build.py` `__main__`, immediately after argv parsing and BEFORE `build()`.
DESIGN, MINE UNDER RULING 37: **the trigger is the CLAIM, found by content — not the filename.**
A volume is gated iff it names `COORDINATES-2.13` AND matches `read from[^.\n]{0,60}at build`.
Both halves are required, and the second is why: main 10213 and Register 5785 NAME the companion
without claiming to read it, so a one-half trigger would have gated two volumes coords.py cannot
check. A rename cannot bypass a content trigger. A MISSING COMPANION IS A FAILURE, NOT A SKIP —
absent the file, the volume's claim about itself is false and the press must not proceed.
VERIFIED, and the failure mode DEMONSTRATED rather than asserted:
  TRIGGER TEST — fires on Spectra ALONE across all six volumes.
  NEGATIVE TEST — 104,474 corrupted to 104,475 in a copy: gate exit 1, both affected sites named
    (Part 0 table and the witness schema line), **press aborted before pandoc ran, no docx written.**
  POSITIVE — gate exit 0 against the shipped volume, 9 sites and all 21 bounds rows.
SPEC-02 IS NOW CLOSED MECHANICALLY: the volume's two self-claims are true of the mechanism, not
merely of the result.

**ref.docx REBUILT — AND HANDOFF-20 §1's RECIPE IS WRONG IN TWO PLACES. CORRECTED HERE.**
  (i)  `<w:sectPr/>` DOES NOT EXIST in pandoc's default document.xml. The serialization is
       `<w:sectPr />`, WITH A SPACE. Matched by ELEMENT NAME with a regex anchor instead.
       This is the space-variant fault the project has met before. Never test for an XML element
       by one literal serialization.
  (ii) "insert `<w:sz w:val="21"/><w:szCs w:val="21"/>` into docDefaults' rPr" WOULD DUPLICATE:
       docDefaults ALREADY carries `<w:sz w:val="24" />` and `<w:szCs w:val="24" />`. They are
       REPLACED, not inserted.
  (iii) AND THE RECIPE IS SILENT ON THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST. docDefaults' fonts are THEME
       attributes — `w:asciiTheme`, `w:hAnsiTheme`, `w:eastAsiaTheme`, `w:cstheme` — which "set
       every font attribute to Georgia" MISSES if read as the plain `w:ascii` family. 48 theme
       attributes were converted to literal Georgia; only 3 plain ones existed. A recipe followed
       literally would have produced a ref.docx that is NOT Georgia at the document default.
VERIFIED IN THE OBJECT: 0 non-Georgia font attrs · 0 theme attrs · one sz at 21 · EntryBody
present · pgSz 12240x15840 · six 1440 margins · zip loads clean. 10,284 bytes.
**CARRY THE CORRECTED RECIPE FORWARD IN PLACE OF §1's.**

**PRESS NOT RUN — NAMED, NOT SILENT.** The Spectra press was attempted and the gate passed; it then
failed on the absent ref.docx (now built) and warns on FIVE absent figures
(figures-compendia/fig-supply.png, fig-channel-map.png, fig-index-final.png, figures/figaddscmargin.png,
figaddscgpin.png). The figures zip was NOT fetched this session. Pressing without it produces an
object with five replaced images, and NO VOLUME CHANGED this chat, so the press buys nothing now.
OWED at chat 20, after the figures are staged.

content.text:
**Row 1.7 carries a bare `|X|`** — and pandoc reads those pipes as cell delimiters. The row splits into five cells in a three-column table, so the statement truncates at "while" and the object `A.derived` is **dropped from the printed table entirely**. A reader loses it. (Row 1.9 was my own print truncation at 3,200 characters, not a defect — checked before saying so.)

Scanning all six volumes for the fault class before repairing anything.

content.text: My probe over-fired: the Mathematical Compendium and IoI rows already escape their pipes as `\|`, correctly — my splitter didn't respect escaping. Re-running it escape-aware, and looking at the one other main-volume table.

def cells(l):
    s=l.strip()
    if s.startswith("|"): s=s[1:]
    if s.endswith("|") and not s.endswith("\\|"): s=s[:-1]
    return re.split(r'(?<!\\)\|', s)
tot=0

# THE METHOD 1.6 — HANDOFF (chat 24 → chat 25), 2026-08-26
Chat: 24. Build described: BUILD-25. Register range: 165–1770.
Those three agree with the files. Register: 1,449 entry headings · 1,474 numbers (all distinct) ·
7 grouped headings · 4 non-numeric front-matter subheads · **5,869 lines (`wc -l` 5868)**.
**ONE VOLUME CHANGED — main, ONE LINE (11275). NO REGISTER ENTRY ADDED.** The change is editorial,
not subject matter, so under Ruling 27 it is recorded as **W-020** in WORKING-REGISTER.md, on
W-001's precedent. **THE AUTHOR SHOULD RULE ON THIS** — see §3.
**Rulings 1–42 plus the R27 Amendment are in force. NO RULING ISSUED THIS CHAT.**

## 0. THE READING GATE — EXECUTE BEFORE ANY OTHER WORK. NO EXCEPTIONS.
It has now run eleven times and found an error inside itself on ten. **Chat 24 found four.**
  G1  `recent_chats n=20`; again with `before=` — n=20 does NOT reach the earliest, it stops at
      Rebuild 4. **23 CHATS: Rebuild 1–12, 13–19, 21, 22, 23, plus one unnumbered chat
      ("Extract transitions from file", 2026-08-26 15:47). THERE IS NO CHAT 20 — the sequence skips
      it. Do not hunt for it.** The old §0 said 21 and listed 22; corrected here to the measured 23.
  G2  Split both BUILD-25 bundles. MEASURE both. Count DECLARED, PAIRED and spurious markers
      SEPARATELY. If a bundle looks absent, RE-LIST; /mnt/project syncs late.
      **THE HANDOFF IS A MEMBER OF THE BUILD IT DESCRIBES.** BUILD-24 was recorded at 83 and measured
      84 for exactly this reason. BUILD-25's count in §1 below was taken AFTER packing, not predicted.
  G3  Read WORKING-REGISTER.md. MEASURE ITS LENGTH FIRST. **`wc -l` RETURNS 2016. The file is
      2,017 LINES — the last line is unterminated, so `wc -l` reports one less. NOT A DISAGREEMENT.**
      VERIFY, do not recite. `sed -n 'a,bp'` does not elide and is cheaper than `view`.
      It carries **RULINGS 27, 28, the R27 Amendment, AND 29–42 — 29 and 30 ARE HERE**, verbatim,
      bold inline at lines 736 and 785. (The old §0 said they were not. They are.)
      Also 114 excised headings (119 numbers, 3 grouped, `### ` lines 30–708) and W-001…W-020.
      **W-015 has no `###` heading — bold inline at line 1648. Present, not missing. And `W-015`
      MATCHES INSIDE `W-015a` at 1721 — guard the probe or it will tell you W-015 has a heading.**
  G4  PRINT THE CERTIFICATE. Until it prints, state NOTHING about the work, change NO file.
      CERT: chats read = N/__ · bundle members = ___ + ___ · rulings = 1–42 + amendment
            · Register entry headings = ____ · Register numbers = ____ · instruments = ____
  G5  VERIFY BUILD IDENTITY, NOT SIZE: `grep -c 'A-Z' index_pages.py` (**3**, was 0 at BUILD-24) and
      `grep -c 'W-020' WORKING-REGISTER.md` (>=1). Either disagrees -> STOP and report.
  **G6 — NEW. CHECK THE TOOL EXISTS BEFORE TRUSTING ITS SILENCE.** `xxd` IS NOT INSTALLED. A test
      built on it fails silently and returns output shaped exactly like an answer. Chat 24's newline
      test reported all eight files identically before this was caught. Use `od -An -tx1`.
  Failure mode: any count RECITED from a prompt rather than READ from a file = gate not passed.

**RECONCILIATIONS — measure once, do not treat as conflicts.** Re-measured at chat 24.
  - Register 1,453 `### ` lines − 4 front-matter subheads = 1,449 entry headings, 1,474 numbers.
    NOT the 1,447/1,472 question held at PR1; that one is untouched and stays held.
  - **EVERY FILE ENDS WITHOUT A NEWLINE — EXCEPT `Transitions.md`, WHICH ENDS `0a`.** Verified with
    `od`, not `xxd`. `wc -l` under-reports by one for every file BUT that one.
    **Main 11,750 · Register 5,868 · Math 3,471 · Physics 861 · IoI 1,947 · Spectra 1,010 ·
    WORKING-REGISTER 2,016 · Transitions 2,288 exactly.** (The old §0 said Register 5,895. Wrong.)
  - Excised: 114 headings, 119 numbers, THREE grouped. 69 A-production · 22 B-session · 23 C-internal.

**THE FALSE STATE — RULING 41 EXPLAINS IT; DO NOT REFUTE IT AGAIN.** Ruling 40-about-F.4.2,
BUILD-26+, HANDOFF-28, regsize.py, ratios.py, pageproof.py, RESTORE-PACKS.md, Register ~1,787 are
residue of chats deleted after a fatal error. **IT ARRIVED AGAIN AT CHAT 24 THROUGH THE MODEL'S
CARRIED MEMORY** — fourth consecutive session, and still the only channel. Expect it; record it;
proceed on the files. COLLISION: a GENUINE Ruling 40 exists (**the tower held entire**,
WORKING-REGISTER line 1619). A "Ruling 40" about F.4.2, withdrawn counts or a 0.09:1 ratio is false.

## 1. INSTRUMENTS — 24 .py. NONE ADDED OR REMOVED. **ONE EDITED: `index_pages.py`.**
**RULING 41 CLOSES THE MISSING-INSTRUMENT QUESTION PERMANENTLY.** guard.py, press_all.py, mkref.py,
figs.py, pageproof.py, ratios.py, regsize.py, indices.py, mathreg.py, mathverify.py, compendium.py,
store_gen.py, RESTORE-PACKS.md lived in deleted chats and are NOT recoverable. Two dispositions:
REBUILT FROM SCRATCH under a ruling, or IGNORED. Do not search Drive. Do not ask the author.
`appf.py` is RETIRED, not deleted — dead code, do not call it. It was NOT called this chat.
**guard.py DOES NOT EXIST.** Its function was served this chat by: one volume changed, one line, and
W-020 recording it in the same build.

**`index_pages.py` — THREE `[A-F]` LITERALS GENERALISED TO `[A-Z]` (lines 19, 66, 82).** Ruling 37.
Appendix G fell outside the hardcoded range and was dropped from the Contents with no warning. See
W-020. **`grep -c 'A-Z' index_pages.py` is now a build discriminator.**

**ref.docx IS NOT A BUNDLE MEMBER and must be rebuilt before any press. USE W-013's RECIPE**
(WORKING-REGISTER ~line 1549). Rebuilt and verified this chat; the three corrections all held.
**W-013 counted 48 theme attributes; this container's pandoc default carries 36.** A different
pandoc, not a wrong W-013 — verify the OBJECT's properties, never the recipe's counts.

**FIGURES — FETCHED AND STAGED. DEBT CLOSED AT FIVE SESSIONS.**
`The_Method_1_6_figures_BUILD13.zip`, Drive `1q7pvnxMPILD9AVoH6XjymZHXX79YzITd`, 6,299,293 bytes,
sha256 `ee423b9ca550a94e7fe0baa41f6ef032`. Unzip into `/home/claude/build/`: `figures/` 49,
`figures-compendia/` 12. **All five previously-absent figures PRESENT; the press warned on none.**
NOT bundle members — refetch each session.

**THE DRIVE LARGE-FILE PATH IS PROVEN — USE IT, DO NOT FEAR IT.** Over ~1 MB the result is written to
`/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<tool_call_id>.json` and never arrives inline. Decode:
`d=json.load(open(p)); inner=json.loads(d[0]['text']); blob=base64.b64decode(inner['content'])`
then verify against the Drive `fileSize`. `pdftotext -layout`, `pdfinfo`, `soffice`, `pandoc`,
`python-docx 1.2.0` all present. **`xxd` is NOT.**

**COORDINATES-2.13 — SUPPLIED, DO NOT ASK AGAIN.** `/mnt/project/COORDINATES-2_13.csv`, 10,912,381
bytes. THE CONNECTOR REFUSES IT (10 MB cap). Not a bundle member. `coords.py` reaches
`/mnt/project/` directly and gates Spectra automatically inside `build.py`.

**PRESS INVOCATIONS.** The digit is LAST in argv; it is `index_pages.py`'s DEPTH.
  main      `python3 build.py The_Method_1_6-2.md OUT/main.docx "The Method 1.6" strip pages 2`
  Register  `python3 build.py ...The_Register-2.md OUT/register.docx "... — The Register" fix 0`
            **NO `pages`. RULING 38. SETTLED TWICE — do not re-derive it a third time.**
  math/phys/ioi/spectra  `python3 build.py <src> OUT/<x>.docx "<title>" pages 2`
  Register afterwards: `soffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir OUT OUT/register.docx`

## 2. WHAT CLOSED THIS CHAT — THE PRESS, AND APPENDIX G PROVED ON THE PAGE
**ALL SIX PRESSED.** main **281 pp** · Register **388 pp** · Math **101** · Physics **26** · IoI **42**
· Spectra **23**. Every page map converged. main: 846 headings mapped 846, 308 locators, 0 unmapped.
**coords.py gate FIRED AND PASSED on Spectra alone** — exit 0, 104,832 CSV rows, 21 bounds rows
summing to 104,499. 50 images embedded (main 33, IoI 8, Spectra 5, Math 2, Physics 2).

**APPENDIX G BROKE TWICE AND BOTH BREAKS WERE FOUND ONLY ON THE PAGE.** Full detail in W-020.
  1. **Dropped from the Contents entirely** by `index_pages.py`'s `[A-F]` literal. The press reported
     845/845 headings mapped and was telling the truth about the 845 it knew of. Instrument, fixed.
  2. **Row 1.7's bare `|X|` read as cell delimiters** — 5 cells in a 3-column table, the statement
     truncated at "while", and **`A.derived` dropped from the printed table.** The table set as three
     columns, so no structural check could see it. Volume, one line, fixed by escaping to `\|X\|`,
     the convention the work already uses in Math, IoI and main's own table at 6398.
**VERIFIED ON THE PAGE AFTER REPAIR:** `Appendix G — Transitions, indexed …… 267` sets in the
Contents; row 1.7 prints whole with `A.derived`; **all 30 locators of the 30-row table reach the
page**, 1.2 through 10.5, header repeating across the break.

**THE FAULT CLASS SCANNED ACROSS ALL SIX VOLUMES — exactly ONE overfull row in the whole work.**
An escape-aware cell count against each table's own header. The first, non-escape-aware scan reported
13; twelve were correctly-escaped rows in Math and IoI. Re-run before anything was reported.

## 3. FOR THE AUTHOR — TWO THINGS, AND ONE IS A RULING
**(a) A VOLUME CHANGED AND NO REGISTER ENTRY RECORDS IT.** The standing directive says a volume may
not change unless a Register entry in the same build records it. Ruling 27 says editorial work is
forbidden from the Register. Row 1.7's pipe escape is editorial — it changes no claim, only whether
the claim reaches the page. I followed **W-001's precedent** (chat 13: five main-volume sites
repaired, recorded in WORKING-REGISTER only) and recorded it as W-020. **If the author wants a
Register entry for volume changes even when editorial, that is a ruling and it is not made.**

**(b) FINDING HELD, NOT REPAIRED — `Index` and `References` have NO page numbers in the main
Contents.** `index_pages.py` line 84 emits them bare, no leader dots, no page. Pre-existing in every
press to date. A reader cannot find the Index from the Contents. Reader-facing, so not mine. **For A6.**

**(c) THE AUTHOR'S STANDING QUESTION ON THE 47 UNCITED T SECTIONS** — answered in chat 24's closing
report, not yet ruled. The proposal on the table: the complete transition table belongs in the Index
of Indices, not as a main-volume appendix. **Appendix G stands either way.** Unruled.

## 4. OPEN, IN ORDER, FOR CHAT 25
1. **THE REMAINING TWELVE STANDING QUESTIONS**, one at a time, few words, no batching.
   HANDOFF-22 §5B carries the list; items 1 and 16 are answered. **NOT STARTED at chats 21, 22, 23, 24.**
2. **PUT RULING 42's SITE LIST TO THE AUTHOR** — 29 non-Register lines (main 10 · Math 12 · IoI 3 ·
   Physics 2 · Spectra 2). Then execute. Whether an editorial removal earns a Register entry is
   §5B item 15 and BLOCKS this. **NOT STARTED at chats 21, 22, 23, 24.**
3. **A4's READER READ** (mechanical layer closed at W-016), then **A5 the Register**, then **A6 the
   main volume LAST.** All findings to WORKING-REGISTER.md, NEVER to the Register.
   **A6 MUST READ APPENDIX G as a reader** — it is now pressed and proved mechanically, but unaudited.
   A6 must also take (b) above. **NOT STARTED at chats 23, 24.**
4. SCHEDULED, NOT NOW: WP-1 Appendix F, WP-2 the Register's front matter, Ruling 31's renumber.

## 5. DO NOT START WITHOUT M's RULING
- **The tower — HELD ENTIRE by Ruling 40 until A4 and A6 report.** Ruling 39 is NOT withdrawn and
  NOT executed; its steps 1–3 STAND AS DONE and are not to be re-derived. ZERO SITES EDITED.
- **Ruling 42's removals** — the site list goes to the author first.
- The 126 unreconciled Spectra rows. The five narrow-bracket FAIL rows named in R1763.
- **Rebuilding ANY deleted instrument — Ruling 41.** `indices.py` matters most.
- The 1,447 / 1,472 count question (HELD by M at PR1 — now 1,449/1,474; report if it moves, do not re-ask).
- Any re-sort of the Spectra channel table (SPEC-06) — reader-visible and press-hazardous.
- The renumber (Ruling 31) and Appendix F's rebuild (Ruling 30) — scheduled, neither open.
- **Register navigation — CLOSED BY RULING 38. Do not raise it again.**
- **The two unexamined Drive PDFs** — `theory_of_everything_expanded_formalism.pdf`
  (`1rMUDhfMyT5sxPxKT3X8it-7ymEdpNvK6`) and `Everything_we_can_see,_touch,_or_detect_using_elec....pdf`
  (`1xKvugHqahCHKs1DsaTlDwCZqmxmR1sna`). For a later part of the project. Do not absorb, cite or act.
- **Whether the 47 uncited T sections should ever enter, and where the whole table belongs.** §3(c).
- `register_cites.py` parses ENTRY BODIES ONLY, so a citation in the Register's front matter is
  invisible to it (this is how 1732 was missed in chat 14). Unrepaired.

## 6. THE STANDING LESSON THIS CHAT ADDS
**NEVER ENCODE A SET AS THE ENUMERATION YOU HAPPEN TO HAVE TODAY.** `[A-F]` was true when it was
written and became false the moment Appendix G existed — and it failed by omission, which reports
nothing. This is the same shape as `<w:sectPr />`'s space and as `T\s§` matching "AT": a test written
against one instance of a class. The general form: **a check must be written against the class, and
a check that can only fail silently must be paired with a count that would move.**

content.text:
**Context is at roughly 90%. Declaring the handoff.** BUILD‑25 is packed and staged; nine files above.

## What closed

**The press, after five sessions owed.** Six volumes: main 281 pp · Register 388 · Math 101 · Physics 26 · IoI 42 · Spectra 23. Every page map converged, the coords gate fired and passed on Spectra alone, 50 images embedded, and — for the first time — **no absent-figure warnings**. The figures fetched clean at 6,299,293 bytes, matching §0 exactly.

**Appendix G broke twice, and both breaks were invisible to every structural check.**

The first: `index_pages.py` had the appendix letters written in as the literal `[A-F]`. Appendix G fell outside it and was dropped from the Contents entirely. The press reported *845 headings mapped 845* and was telling the truth — about the 845 it knew existed. Nothing failed. It just wasn't there.

The second is the one worth your attention. Row 1.7 of the table contained a bare `|X|`. Pandoc read those pipes as cell delimiters, split the row into five cells in a three-column table, truncated the statement at "while", and **dropped `A.derived` from the printed table**. The table still set as three clean columns. A reader would have seen a well-formed row whose third column read "X" and would have lost the object the row exists to name. §0 predicted the shape and the page is where it showed.

Both repaired, both verified on the page: `Appendix G — Transitions, indexed …… 267` sets in the Contents, row 1.7 prints whole with `A.derived`, and all thirty locators reach the page.

**One thing you should rule on.** The row‑1.7 repair changed a volume, and I recorded it as W‑020 in the working register rather than as a Register entry — following W‑001's precedent, since a pipe escape changes no claim, only whether the claim reaches the page. Your standing directive says a volume may not change without a Register entry in the same build. Ruling 27 says editorial work is forbidden from the Register. I took the precedent; if you want the directive read strictly, that is a ruling and it isn't made.

**Held, not repaired:** `Index` and `References` carry no page numbers in the main Contents. Pre‑existing in every press. A reader can't find the Index from the Contents. Reader‑facing, so it goes to A6, not to me.

**Shortfall, named:** three of four open items untouched — the twelve standing questions, Ruling 42's site list, and A4/A5/A6. Fourth consecutive session for the first two. The press took the chat.

## Your question

Yes, I agree — with one distinction that I think is the whole of it.

**Appendix G is not the transition table.** It is a dependency index: thirty rows, each an address for something *this book leans on*. Its value to a reader is that every row is load‑bearing. Put all seventy‑seven sections there and the thirty that matter are buried among forty‑seven the book never uses — the appendix stops being an address and becomes a reproduction. That is exactly the filler your compendium standard rules out.

The complete table is a different object with a different function: an index of a body of work. The Index of Indices is the volume whose subject is precisely that. Taxonomically it belongs there, and Appendix G should stay exactly as it is and name the IoI as where the whole lives.

Two things to price before you rule. The IoI cites *Transitions* nowhere at present — measured at chat 23 — so this makes it the first volume to carry T whole, and its self‑description and counts would move with it. And more sharply: **1770 says the forty‑seven do not enter.** Putting them in the IoI *is* them entering, in a different volume. That supersedes part of 1770 — which under the append‑only rule means a new Register entry citing it, never an edit to it.

## Upload and retire

Upload both **BUILD‑25** bundles and **HANDOFF‑26**. Retire the **BUILD‑24** bundles and **HANDOFF‑25**. The **BUILD‑12** bundles are still sitting in the mount — they were marked for retirement at chat 23 and have now been dead for twelve chats. Leave `COORDINATES-2_13.csv`, the PNGs and `Transitions-1.md`.

## Prompt for chat 25

> Prime Handoff Directive — state at 90% and hand off complete. Prime Zeno Directive — fetch → read → analyse → close flags → report; close each segment before the next.
>
> The Method 1.6 — chat 25. Execute §0 of HANDOFF-26 before anything else and print the certificate. §0 has a new **G6: check a tool exists before trusting its silence — `xxd` is not installed and a test built on it fails silently**. G5's discriminators are `grep -c 'A-Z' index_pages.py` (3) and `grep -c W-020 WORKING-REGISTER.md`. G1 needs a `before=` page — n=20 stops at Rebuild 4, and there are **23** chats. State no member count in this prompt — measure both BUILD-25 bundles at G2, and note the handoff is a member of the build it describes. Rulings 1–42 plus the R27 Amendment are in force; none was issued at chat 24. Register: 1,449 entry headings, 1,474 numbers, 165–1770. 24 instruments, two edited at chat 24.
>
> Ruling 41 explains the false state — do not test it, do not refute it. It arrives through your carried memory, not the prompt. A genuine Ruling 40 exists (the tower held entire); a "Ruling 40" about F.4.2 or a 0.09:1 ratio is the false one. There is no chat 20. WORKING-REGISTER **does** carry Rulings 29 and 30, bold inline — the old §0 said otherwise and was wrong.
>
> The press is done and Appendix G is proved on the page. Do not re-press unless a volume changes.
>
> Open in order, and **the first two have now gone unstarted for four consecutive chats**: (1) the remaining twelve standing questions, one at a time, few words, no batching — HANDOFF-22 §5B carries the list; (2) Ruling 42's 29-line site list to me, then execute; (3) A4's reader read, then A5, then A6 last — A6 must read Appendix G as a reader and must take the Index/References Contents finding in HANDOFF-26 §3(b).
>
> The tower is held entire by Ruling 40. Do not start the 126 Spectra rows, the five narrow-bracket FAIL rows, any re-sort of the Spectra channel table, the renumber, or Appendix F's rebuild without my ruling. Do not absorb, cite or act on the two unexamined Drive PDFs.

Two rulings are waiting on you, and neither blocks chat 25 from opening: whether an editorial volume change earns a Register entry (HANDOFF‑26 §3a), and where the complete transition table goes — which, if it goes to the Index of Indices, needs a new entry citing 1770 rather than any change to it.
